title: Confirmed Python project
source_request: Build the software described and confirmed by the user.
requirements: Provide automated tests, project documentation, and sat-project.json.

acceptance_criteria.description: The delivered project satisfies the confirmed user outcomes.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Inspect the immutable implementation and tests during independent review.

acceptance_criteria.description: The project supplies a validated setup, start, and test command contract, and its exact start command is directly runnable from the project root without additional arguments or edits.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run CHECK_PROJECT_CONTRACT, then independently probe the exact start argv with no appended arguments.

acceptance_criteria.description: The project's automated pytest suite is importable from the clean quality workspace and passes through the documented post-setup command.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run CHECK_PROJECT_TESTS and verify the exact uv run pytest command after setup.

acceptance_criteria.description: The Python source compiles and passes the pinned linter.

The README explains setup, usage, tests, and known limitations, shows the exact setup, start, and test commands from sat-project.json, and keeps any explicitly claimed JSON example output consistent with the running project.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run CHECK_PROJECT_CONTRACT and CHECK_EXACT_PROJECT_COMMANDS, then independently review documentation claims.

constraints: Use the supplied local Python 3.12 execution profile.
Do not require runtime network access or credentials.

Keep sat-project.json setup exactly ["uv", "sync", "--dev"] and test exactly ["uv", "run", "pytest"]; replace only the start placeholder with a project-specific argv beginning ["uv", "run"]. The exact start argv must run after setup in a clean committed copy without a README-only sample file or other untracked fixture; use the CLI's no-argument interactive entry point when an input path is required.

Make the exact start argv directly usable from the project root without extra arguments or configuration edits; a CLI must include a safe default input or interactive flow and a service must start with a complete local configuration.

When a CLI promises machine-readable stdout, keep all interactive prompts and diagnostics on stderr. If the exact start argv waits for a file path, send one through stdin in tests and verify stdout contains only the documented result, not prompt text; also test Ctrl-C without a traceback.

Keep tests importable when CHECK_PROJECT_TESTS invokes pytest from the clean quality workspace before setup, including explicit pytest pythonpath configuration for a src layout, and also pass the exact post-setup command uv run pytest. A test launched from a temporary directory must not assume that uv can find the project's console script there without project metadata; invoke an explicit source/module entry point or run from a correctly installed project context.

Commit uv.lock as portable dependency-resolution metadata: do not record absolute paths, file: sources, parent-directory dependencies, or runtime-image-local package paths; in the SAT sandbox, use sat-project-lock after changing dependency metadata and before committing.

Show the exact setup, start, and test shell commands in README.md; headings such as Installation, Usage, and Testing are valid and do not need the literal words setup or start. If README.md claims an Expected JSON output, place its label immediately before the bash block or between the bash and JSON blocks. Use exactly two executable lines inside that shell block: one echo -e, printf %s, or bounded printf-format root-file fixture, then the exact start command with optional arguments. Prefer the portable fixture printf '%s' 'hello world' > example.txt with literal UTF-8 text; for mixed line endings use printf 'café
über line
' > example.txt. Only 
, , 	, and \ escapes are supported in a format string; no hexadecimal escapes, \c, or combined echo flags such as -ne. Put explanatory comments outside the fenced shell block; the clean-copy gate executes and compares the JSON. For a file code-point count, preserve decoded CRLF bytes and test mixed CRLF/LF input.
assumptions: This template defines criterion IDs; each product run supplies user-confirmed content.
